To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Florida norms are the first to provide a comprehensive set of psychometric norms for pre-cardiac transplant evaluations.
the Florida cohort is a large population of pre-transplantation candidates with a high degree of homogeneity and a low degree of heterogeneity.

(a) The Florida cohort is the largest sample of pre-cardiac transplant candidates to have their psychological test results published; (b) The Florida cohort's psychological test performance is comparable to that of the general population, with the exception of the MMPI-2 and the MCMI-II, which were found to be elevated for the Florida cohort; (c) The Florida cohort was not found to be significantly different from other cohorts of pre-cardiac transplantation candidates on any of the psychological tests administered
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of normative data for a variety of psychological tests.
the development of psychometric norms that can be used to assess the psychological functioning of patients with advanced cardiopulmonary disease.
the development of psychometric norms for the evaluation of pre-cardiac transplantation candidates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these norms are an important step in providing a standard of practice that can be used to evaluate the utility of psychological tests for the pre-cardiac transplantation evaluation.
these norms provide a standard of practice that should be adopted by transplant psychologists in the evaluation of cardiac transplant candidates.
these norms are the best available for use by the transplant psychologist.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of psychological test data in the context of pre-cardiac transplantation evaluation should be based on a sound rationale, and the psychologist should be familiar with the psychometric properties and the normative data for the specific test(s) being used.
these norms are a significant contribution to the field of clinical health psychology and the practice of transplantation psychology.
the use of psychological testing in pre-cardiac transplantation evaluation has become an important part of the multidisciplinary evaluation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a comprehensive battery of psychological tests is an important component of pre-cardiac transplant evaluations.

the use of psychological test batteries that have appropriate norms for transplant candidates will allow the transplant psychologist a more accurate and precise evaluation of the candidate's current level of functioning and a forecast of future functioning after transplantation.
